newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine positive ahead of Chernobyl shutdown talks.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine positive ahead of Chernobyl shutdown talks.

text.p: Ukraine's top Chernobyl negotiator said on Monday he expected the Group of Seven countries and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to pay millions of dollars to close the power plant.

Chernobyl will be on the G-7's agenda at its Denver summit next month when it considers a $780 million project to stabilise the concrete "sarcophagus" enclosing the ruined fourth reactor, scene in 1986 of the world's worst nuclear accident.

The EBRD board is to decide at the end of this month on payment to construct two new reactors at the Khmelnytsky and Rivne nuclear power stations in western Ukraine, to replace power lost by Chernobyl's closure.
"We hope that the decisions will be positive," Yuri Kostenko, also environment minister, told a news conference after returning from meetings with the EBRD board in London.
"As part of the deal Ukraine must be able to build the two reactors," Kostenko said. "The value of the project is $1.2 billion."
When the fourth reactor at Chernobyl, 150 km (80 miles) from Kiev, exploded it sent a radioactive cloud over the neighbouring countries of Belarus and Russia and over parts of Europe.
Ukraine has been working on an agreement with the G7 since promising to close the site by 2000 in exchange for $3.1 billion in grants and credits.
Kostenko repeated previous statements that the EBRD's refusal to fund construction of the two reactors could jeopardise the closure date.
"Today everything depends on the EBRD's position," he said. "If the EBRD refuses, or provides only partial funding, Ukraine will be forced to review its schedule for closing Chernobyl."

The project to stabilise the crumbling sarcophagus, feared to be leaking radiation, would be implemented to 2005 and included stabilising the structure's walls, constructing shields over fuel deposits still in the sarcophagus until they can be safely removed and building some sort of shelter over it.
